newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus economy looking up in 97 - finance minister.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus economy looking up in 97 - finance minister.

text.p: The outlook of Cyprus' economy in 1997 is considerably better than last year with tourism and other sectors of the economy showing encouraging signs, the finance minister said on Monday.

"The estimates of the CTO (Cyprus Tourism Organisation) and of other interested parties is that bookings are fluctuating at 1996 levels with prospects of improvement," Cypriot Finance Minister Christodoulos Christodoulou told a news conference.
Christodoulou put his optimism in the "favourable exchange rate of foreign currencies against the Cyprus pound" and in a large-scale campaign promoting Cyprus in tourism markets.
A large number of the estimated two million tourists who visit Cyprus each year are from Britain.
Tourism is the island's main money spinner, representing some 21 percent of its gross national product.

"We also have encouraging signs from manufacturing where the incentives and grants scheme for exports and technological improvement has started to show results," Christodoulou said, referring to a series of government-backed schemes announced in February to boost exports.
Christodoulou said favourable economic conditions reflected the forecast that GDP would grow between three and 3.5 percent in 1997.
The GDP growth estimate for 1996 is 2.5 percent.
